question.problem: Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=\frac{3x}{2}+6,$ $y=-3x-3$ and $y=0.$ Express ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/8dad5cdaa9fdcaf0293773c53a0b5ab58d7d98aea0099af0a9ba616e72759129.png)

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/a0b5bfe05214df5f59a563677bd6b4f7dfd85be4d8e27fd4d7b31f87a679cd2b.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-4\le x\le -2,\,0\le y\le \frac{3x}{2}+6\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le -1,\,0\le y\le -3x-3\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-4}^{-2}{\int }_{0}^{3x/2+6}f(x,y)\,dy\,dx+{\int }_{-2}^{-1}{\int }_{0}^{-3x-3}f(x,y)\,dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$
